info.title: BallotData API
info.summary: U.S. ballots, endorsers and endorsements, and a live stream of endorsement changes.
info.description:
Ballot races (elections, contests and their choices), endorsers and endorsements across the U.S., who holds office now, and a stream of endorsement changes.

Everything is JSON over HTTPS. Send your API key on every request as `Authorization: Bearer ebk_…`. Lists are paged: `{ "data": [...], "next_cursor": "…" }`; pass `cursor` for the next page. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "request_id" } }`.

To find the ballot at an address, send it to `POST /v1/ballot`; the address is used for that request only and never stored.

tags.name: Elections
tags.description: States, elections and coverage: what there is to ask about.

tags.name: Contests
tags.description: The races on a ballot and their choices: candidates, or Yes/No for a measure. Contests carry their voting rules: vote for one, vote for N (votes_allowed), ranked choice (ranks_allowed), or yes/no, and their election results once a source has them: official counts from election offices, certified returns compiled by researchers for past elections, or a party’s announcement of the winner, always with the source’s URL.

tags.name: Endorsers
tags.description: Who endorses: unions, newspapers, parties, clubs, advocacy groups and officials, by category and home state.

tags.name: Endorsements
tags.description: Who each endorser backs in each race, and every change to those endorsements.

tags.name: Candidates
tags.description: The people on the ballot, every endorsement each one received, and where they stand on common issues.

tags.name: Officeholders
tags.description: Who holds each seat now, from Open States.

tags.name: Offices
tags.description: Seats that last across elections and redistricting, who held each since 2020, and whether each result changed hands.

tags.name: Stream
tags.description: Every endorsement added, changed or removed, as Server-Sent Events or by polling. Needs the stream:read scope and a plan that includes the stream.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description: Saved filters for the stream and events. Reading needs stream:read; changing needs subscriptions:write.

bearer.description: An API key from the console, as Authorization: Bearer ebk_…

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: The same key in an X-API-Key header, for clients that can’t set Authorization.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per minute on your plan.

X-Daily-Limit.description: Requests allowed per UTC day, on plans with a daily cap.

X-Request-Id.description: This request’s id. Quote it when you write to us.

Error.description: The body of every error response.

x-enumDescriptions.missing_api_key: No API key was sent. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <key> (or X-API-Key).
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_api_key: The key isn’t one we issued: mistyped, cut off, or from another site.
x-enumDescriptions.revoked_api_key: The key was revoked in the console. Use another key.
x-enumDescriptions.expired_api_key: The key passed the expiry date set on it.
x-enumDescriptions.ip_not_allowed: The key is limited to certain addresses and this request came from another.
x-enumDescriptions.account_pending: The account is waiting for approval.
x-enumDescriptions.account_suspended: The account is suspended. Write to us.
x-enumDescriptions.insufficient_scope: The key lacks the scope this endpoint needs (data:read, stream:read or subscriptions:write).
x-enumDescriptions.no_access: The account’s purchases don’t include this part of the API (the stream, for example), or they have ended.
x-enumDescriptions.outside_purchase: The record is in a state or election the account hasn’t bought. The message says what it does cover.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_parameter: A parameter has a value we can’t use: the message names it.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_cursor: The cursor isn’t one we gave out. Pass next_cursor back exactly as you got it.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_filter: A stream filter parameter is invalid: the message says which.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_json: The request body isn’t valid JSON.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_subscription: The subscription’s name or filter is invalid: the message says which.
x-enumDescriptions.body_too_large: The request body is over 100 KB.
x-enumDescriptions.not_found: Nothing has that id or slug.
x-enumDescriptions.address_not_found: POST /v1/ballot: the Census Bureau’s geocoder found no such address (or the point is outside the U.S.). Check the spelling and include the city and state or ZIP code.
x-enumDescriptions.subscription_not_found: No subscription in your account has that id or name.
x-enumDescriptions.conflict: A subscription with that name already exists in your account.
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_requests: Too many requests from one address. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_failures: Too many requests with a missing or wrong key from one address. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
x-enumDescriptions.rate_limit_exceeded: Over your plan’s requests a minute. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
x-enumDescriptions.daily_limit_exceeded: Over your plan’s requests a day (the day is UTC).
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_streams: Your account already has as many streams open as its plan allows.
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_lookups: Over 60 ballot lookups (POST /v1/ballot) a minute for the account. Wait for Retry-After seconds.
x-enumDescriptions.cursor_expired: The cursor or since time is older than the 7 days of changes the stream keeps. Start again with from=earliest, and catch up with GET /v1/changes.
x-enumDescriptions.warming_up: The stream is still loading on this server. Try again in a few seconds.
x-enumDescriptions.server_busy: This server has too many open streams. Try again.
x-enumDescriptions.not_available: This data isn’t loaded yet (officeholders or offices, for example). Try again later.
x-enumDescriptions.geocoder_unavailable: POST /v1/ballot: the Census Bureau’s geocoder isn’t answering. Try again in a minute.
x-enumDescriptions.internal_error: Something went wrong on our side. Quote request_id when you write to us.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain English.

request_id.description: Quote this when you write to us. Also sent as the X-Request-Id header.

PresidentialVote.description: The presidential vote within one district in one election year.

dem_votes.description: Votes for the Democratic nominee for president in the district.

rep_votes.description: Votes for the Republican nominee for president in the district.

total_votes.description: All votes for president in the district, every candidate and write-ins.

dem_two_party_pct.description: The Democratic share of the two-party vote, 0 to 100: 100 × dem_votes / (dem_votes + rep_votes). Subtract 50 for the usual lean measure; the Republican share is 100 minus it.

method.description: How the district’s count was made: official_district, official_county, statewide (or aggregated_precincts, reserved).

x-enumDescriptions.official_district: An election office published the presidential vote for this district itself (California’s Statement of Vote supplement, for example).
x-enumDescriptions.official_county: The district is a county: the county’s official presidential returns.
x-enumDescriptions.statewide: The district is the whole state: the state’s official presidential returns.
x-enumDescriptions.aggregated_precincts: Official precinct returns summed to the district. Reserved: no rows use it yet.

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

DistrictPartisanship.description: The district’s partisan lean, as the presidential vote in it: the control most election studies use. Only official counts for exactly the district’s area (a state, a county, or a district an election office reported); never estimated from other areas.

president_2016.description: The 2016 presidential vote in the district; null where we have no official count for it.

president_2020.description: The 2020 presidential vote in the district; null where we have no official count for it.

president_2024.description: The 2024 presidential vote in the district; null where we have no official count for it.

DistrictDemographics.description: The U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey 5-year estimates for the Census areas that make up the district (public domain). This product uses Census Bureau data but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.

acs_year.description: The last year of the American Community Survey 5-year estimates: 2024 means 2020-2024.

citizen_voting_age_population.description: U.S. citizens 18 and over (ACS B05003): the usual denominator for turnout by population.

median_household_income.description: Median household income in dollars (ACS B19013). null for a district made of several Census areas, since medians can’t be combined.

median_age.description: Median age in years (ACS B01002). null for a district made of several Census areas.

pct_bachelors_or_higher.description: Share of people 25 and over with a bachelor’s degree or higher, 0 to 100 (ACS B15003).

pct_white_alone_not_hispanic.description: Share of people who are white alone and not Hispanic or Latino, 0 to 100 (ACS B03002).

pct_black_alone.description: Share of people who are Black or African American alone, Hispanic or not, 0 to 100 (ACS B03002).

pct_asian_alone.description: Share of people who are Asian alone, Hispanic or not, 0 to 100 (ACS B03002).

pct_hispanic.description: Share of people who are Hispanic or Latino, of any race, 0 to 100 (ACS B03002).

pct_foreign_born.description: Share of people born outside the United States, 0 to 100 (ACS B05002).

pct_owner_occupied.description: Share of occupied housing units lived in by their owners, 0 to 100 (ACS B25003).

pct_below_poverty.description: Share of people whose poverty status is determined who are below the poverty line, 0 to 100 (ACS B17001).

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

Turnout.description: Registered voters and ballots cast in the contest’s jurisdiction (a state, or a county, city or town with its own election board) for this election: the denominator for turnout and roll-off. From the U.S. Election Assistance Commission’s Election Administration and Voting Survey for 2020, 2022 and 2024, and from state election offices for 2026.

registered_voters.description: Registered voters in the jurisdiction, as the source counts them (the EAC’s survey counts active and inactive registrants); null where the source gives none, as in North Dakota, which has no registration.

ballots_cast.description: Voters who cast a ballot that was counted, as the source reports it.

turnout_pct.description: The source’s own turnout percentage when it prints one, else ballots_cast / registered_voters × 100. Never against the voting-age population.

status.description: unofficial while the counts can still change; certified once canvassed.

x-enumDescriptions.unofficial: Election-night and canvass counts: still changing. We read them again every day until they’re certified.
x-enumDescriptions.certified: The canvass is certified: the final official count.

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

BackgroundSource.description: One background fact with its source.

attribute.description: Which fact: held_elected_office, prior_office, gender or veteran.

x-enumDescriptions.held_elected_office: Whether the candidate held elected office before: value true. We never record false, so an absence means unknown.
x-enumDescriptions.prior_office: An elected office the candidate held, by its title (value).
x-enumDescriptions.gender: The candidate’s gender as an official roster or the candidate’s own words state it (value: woman, man or nonbinary).
x-enumDescriptions.veteran: The candidate served in the U.S. armed forces, as an official roster or the candidate’s own words state it (value true).

value.description: The value: true, an office title, or woman, man or nonbinary.

basis.description: What it rests on: our_results, officeholder_record, official_roster or candidate_statement.

x-enumDescriptions.our_results: Our own election results: the candidate won an election to the office.
x-enumDescriptions.officeholder_record: Our officeholder records (Open States, CC0): the candidate holds or held the seat.
x-enumDescriptions.official_roster: An official roster: the Congressional Directory, or the congress-legislators list of members of Congress.
x-enumDescriptions.candidate_statement: The candidate’s own words on their campaign website, quoted in quote.

quote.description: The candidate’s own words, one sentence, for a candidate_statement (or the roster’s words for military service).

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

CandidateBackground.description: Three facts research on endorsements controls for: prior elected office, gender and military service. Only as our results, an officeholder record, an official roster or the candidate’s own words state them. A null means unknown. We don’t collect race, ethnicity, religion or sexual orientation.

held_elected_office.description: true when the candidate held elected office before (our results, officeholder records or an official roster show it); null where we don’t know. Never false: no source shows a negative.

prior_offices.description: Elected offices the candidate held, by title. Empty where we know of none.

gender.description: woman, man or nonbinary, only where an official roster or the candidate’s own words state it; null otherwise. Never inferred from a name or a photo.

x-enumDescriptions.woman: A woman, as an official roster or the candidate’s own words state it.
x-enumDescriptions.man: A man, as an official roster or the candidate’s own words state it.
x-enumDescriptions.nonbinary: Nonbinary, as the candidate’s own words state it.

veteran.description: true when an official roster or the candidate’s own words say they served in the U.S. armed forces; null otherwise (not false).

sources.description: Every fact above, each with its source.

IdeologyScore.description: One published ideology estimate for the candidate. Its authors’ estimate from their own method, not a fact about the person, and neither an endorsement nor a rating.

measure.description: Which published measure: dime_cfscore (loaded) or dw_nominate and shor_mccarty (not loaded; their terms don’t allow commercial use).

x-enumDescriptions.dime_cfscore: Bonica’s DIME campaign-finance score (CFscore): candidates and donors on one left-right scale estimated from who gives money to whom. Negative is left, positive is right.
x-enumDescriptions.dw_nominate: Voteview DW-NOMINATE, from roll-call votes in Congress. Not loaded: its terms don’t allow commercial use.
x-enumDescriptions.shor_mccarty: Shor and McCarty state legislator scores. Not loaded: its license is non-commercial.

score.description: The score: for dime_cfscore, roughly -2 to 2, negative left and positive right.

second_dimension.description: A second dimension, for measures that have one; null for dime_cfscore.

period.description: The years the estimate covers, as the source gives them (dime_cfscore: 1979-2024).

person_key.description: The source’s own key for the person: the FEC candidate id for dime_cfscore.

license.description: The license the source is published under: ODC-BY 1.0 for DIME, which asks that you cite it (see /docs/research).

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

CandidateIdeology.description: Published ideology estimates for the candidate, matched on their FEC candidate id. Cite DIME when you use dime_cfscore: Bonica, Adam. 2024. Database on Ideology, Money in Politics, and Elections: Public version 4.0. Stanford University Libraries. https://data.stanford.edu/dime.

dime_cfscore.description: The candidate’s DIME CFscore (Bonica, DIME v4.0, ODC-BY 1.0): one left-right scale from who gives money to whom, negative left and positive right; null where DIME has none (it covers candidates with an FEC id who raised money).

scores.description: Every score we hold for the candidate, with its source and license.

EndorserFactSource.description: One endorser fact with its source.

x-enumDescriptions.fec_committee_id: A Federal Election Commission committee id (C followed by eight digits), from the FEC committee master files.
x-enumDescriptions.ein: The IRS employer identification number (nine digits), from the IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File.
x-enumDescriptions.irs_subsection: The tax-exemption section the IRS lists, such as 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(5).
x-enumDescriptions.union_members: Members the union reported on its latest Department of Labor (OLMS) annual report.
x-enumDescriptions.olms_file_number: The union’s Department of Labor (OLMS) file number.
x-enumDescriptions.founded_year: The year the organization says it was founded, from its own About page.
x-enumDescriptions.parent_organization: The organization it says it is an affiliate or chapter of, from its own About page.

value.description: The value as the source gives it.

as_of.description: The date the fact was true per its source: the end of the report period for union members, the IRS file’s posting date, or the day we read the file or page.

retrieved_on.description: When we read it from the source.

EndorserFacts.description: Identifiers and size, to join other data and weigh an endorsement by who made it: from the FEC, the IRS and the Department of Labor (U.S. government works), and the endorser’s own About page. A null means we have none.

fec_committee_ids.description: Federal Election Commission committee ids (C########) of the endorser’s political committees, from the FEC committee master files 2020-2026. Empty where we found none.

ein.description: IRS employer identification number, nine digits.

irs_subsection.description: The tax-exemption section the IRS lists, such as 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(5).

union_members.description: Members the union reported on its latest Department of Labor annual report (LM-2, LM-3 or LM-4).

union_members_as_of.description: The end of the report period union_members is for.

olms_file_number.description: The union’s Department of Labor (OLMS) file number.

founded_year.description: The year the organization says it was founded.

parent_organization.description: The organization it says it is an affiliate or chapter of.

sources.description: Every fact above, each with its source and date; older union member counts too.

Election.description: The election the contest is in.

slug.description: Election slug, used in elections= filters: <state>-<date>-<type>.

state.description: State; null for a multi-state election.

x-enumDescriptions.general: A general election: the November election (or a state’s regular election day) that fills offices and decides measures.
x-enumDescriptions.primary: A primary: voters choose each party’s nominee, or (in top-two and Louisiana-style states) the candidates who go on to the general.
x-enumDescriptions.special: A special election held outside the regular schedule, usually to fill a vacancy or decide a measure.
x-enumDescriptions.special_primary: The primary for a special election.
x-enumDescriptions.runoff: A runoff between the leading candidates when no one won the earlier round outright (the share needed is in the contest’s details.majority_required or vote_required).
x-enumDescriptions.consolidated: Several jurisdictions’ elections held together on one ballot (a city and school election on the same day, for example); details.consolidated_with names them.

x-enumDescriptions.none: No primary system is recorded for this election.
x-enumDescriptions.closed: Only voters registered with a party may vote in its primary.
x-enumDescriptions.semi_closed: A party’s registered voters, plus unaffiliated voters who choose that party’s ballot.
x-enumDescriptions.open: Any registered voter may choose any one party’s ballot.
x-enumDescriptions.top_two: Every candidate is on one primary ballot whatever their party, and the top two go on to the general (Washington, California).
x-enumDescriptions.top_four: Every candidate is on one primary ballot, and the top four go on to a ranked-choice general (Alaska).
x-enumDescriptions.nonpartisan: Candidates run without party labels; the leading candidates go on, or a majority wins outright.

details.description: Voting rules for the election. Only keys that apply are present.

all_mail.description: Every voter is mailed a ballot.

ranked_choice.description: Some contests in this election use ranked choice voting.

fusion_voting.description: Candidates can appear on more than one party’s line (New York, Connecticut).

primary.description: Which primary, where a state holds several.

consolidated_with.description: Elections held on the same ballot: a name, or a list of names.

runoff_date.description: Date of a runoff, if one is needed.

top_two_primary_date.description: Date of the top-two primary that chose these candidates.

historical.description: A past election kept for its results and history (the November 5, 2024 general, for example). Never shown to voters on endorsedby.org.

result_count.description: Contests on the ballot with a result.

District.description: The district a contest is voted in.

id.description: District id. Matches an officeholder’s district_id.

ocd_id.description: Open Civic Data division id, used in districts= filters.

x-enumDescriptions.county: A county (a parish in Louisiana, a borough in Alaska) or a district within one.

x-enumDescriptions.school: A school district, community college district, or a trustee area within one.
x-enumDescriptions.special: A special district: water, fire, hospital, park, transit, port, conservation and the like.

x-enumDescriptions.anc_smd: A single-member district of a Washington, D.C. Advisory Neighborhood Commission. Example: ANC 1A01.
x-enumDescriptions.annexation_area: The area a proposed annexation would add to a city. Example: Tucker annexation area (SB 622).

x-enumDescriptions.appraisal_district: A property appraisal district. Example: Collin Central Appraisal District.
x-enumDescriptions.assistance_district: A county assistance district (Texas), proposed or in place. Example: Carson County Assistance District (proposed; Carson County outside Panhandle, White Deer, Groom, Skellytown and Fritch).
x-enumDescriptions.board_district: A member district of a local board (a city, utility or similar board). Example: Hot Springs Board District 2.

x-enumDescriptions.board_of_equalization: A district of a state board of equalization (California’s tax board). Example: State Board of Equalization District 2.

x-enumDescriptions.board_of_review_district: A district of a county property-tax board of review. Example: Cook County Board of Review District 1.
x-enumDescriptions.cemetery_district: A cemetery district. Example: Chugwater Cemetery District.
x-enumDescriptions.chancery_court_district: A chancery court district (Mississippi, Tennessee). Example: 1st Chancery Court District.

x-enumDescriptions.circuit_court: A circuit court’s circuit. Example: 6th Judicial Circuit.

x-enumDescriptions.circuit_court_district_subdistrict: A subdistrict that elects one circuit judge. Example: Circuit Court Subdistrict 4-1.
x-enumDescriptions.city: A whole city. Example: City of Oakland.

x-enumDescriptions.college: A community college district. Example: Grossmont-Cuyamaca Community College District.
x-enumDescriptions.college_district: A community college district. Example: Collin County Community College District.
x-enumDescriptions.commission: A county commission, or a district of one. Example: Clay County Commission, Eastern District.

website.description: Website, from Wikidata or (for an incumbent) the official site.

mailing_address.description: Campaign committee mailing address, from its FEC filing.

social.description: Social accounts, from Wikidata, an incumbent’s official accounts, or the campaign’s own website. Only keys we found are present.

sources.description: Where each contact detail came from.

cycle.description: Two-year FEC cycle, by its last year: 2026 = 2025–2026.

cash_on_hand.description: Cash on hand at coverage_end, dollars.

debts.description: Debts owed by the campaign, dollars.

coverage_end.description: The date the totals run through.

source_url.description: The FEC page for these totals.

Choice.description: A line a voter can mark: a candidate, or a Yes/No answer.

id.description: Choice id: the choice_id endorsements refer to.

label.description: As printed: the candidate’s ballot name, or Yes / No.

measure_answer.description: yes or no for a measure or retention question; null for a candidate.

x-enumDescriptions.yes: The Yes line of a measure or retention question. On an endorsement: the endorser says vote Yes.
x-enumDescriptions.no: The No line. On an endorsement: the endorser says vote No.

withdrawn.description: The candidate withdrew but is still printed on the ballot.

incumbent.description: The candidate holds this seat now: true or false where we know, null where we don’t yet (and for a measure answer).

vote_meaning.description: For a measure answer: what a Yes (or No) vote means, as the election office words it.

endorsement_count.description: Endorsers who endorsed this choice (for a measure: who back this answer).

candidate.description: The candidate; null for a measure answer.

party.description: The party (or party preference) printed beside the name.

party_label.description: The party text exactly as printed, where it differs (fusion lines, top-two preferences).

result.description: This choice’s votes, once the contest has a result; null before then.

ChoiceResult.description: One choice’s line in the result.

votes.description: Votes for this choice. null only on a party-reported result, which names a winner without counts.

vote_pct.description: Share of the contest’s votes, 0 to 100, as the source gives it (three decimals).

winner.description: true for a winner (for vote-for-N, each of the N), false for a choice that lost; null when not decided yet or not stated, such as a race headed to a runoff.

label.description: As the source reports it: a write-in’s name, “Write-in”, or another line not on the printed ballot.

status.description: unofficial (election-night and canvass counts, still changing) or certified (the canvass is certified).

url.description: Where it was published: the contest’s own results page where the source has one. Every result has one.

contest_name.description: The contest’s name in the source, which may differ from the printed title.

updated_at.description: When the source last updated it, if it says.

official_url.description: For a compiled result, the state’s own certified results, where we have them.

more_sources.description: Further announcements of the same result (party-reported results that more than one party published).

notes.description: Anything else about the result, such as how a ranked-choice winner was decided.

source_kind.description: Where the result comes from: official (a state, county, city or federal election office), compiled (certified official returns compiled by a research group, such as the MIT Election Data and Science Lab’s precinct returns, summed to the contest) or party (a state or national party’s own announcement of the winner, with no vote counts; replaced as soon as an official result appears).

x-enumDescriptions.official: A state, county, city or federal election office.
x-enumDescriptions.compiled: Certified official returns compiled by a research group (the MIT Election Data and Science Lab’s precinct returns), summed to the contest. Used for past elections; official_url links to the state’s own results where we have them.

party_reported.description: true when the result is a party’s announcement (source_kind party), not an official count.

decided.description: The source names at least one winner. false while counts are still coming in, for a race headed to a runoff, or where the source doesn’t say.

total_votes.description: Votes cast in the contest: the printed choices plus write-ins. null on a party-reported result.

precincts_reporting.description: Precincts counted so far, where the source says.

precincts_total.description: Precincts in the contest, where the source says.

winners.description: The choices marked winner, most votes first. Empty until the source names one.

margin.description: The deciding margin; null without votes for both places (a party-reported winner, an uncontested race). While a count is unofficial it is the current lead.

choices.description: Every choice with a result line, most votes first.

url.description: Where it was published. Every result has one.

contest_name.description: The contest’s name in the source, which may differ from the printed title.

updated_at.description: When the source last updated it, if it says.

official_url.description: For a compiled result, the state’s own certified results, where we have them.

seat_change.description: Whether the incumbent kept the seat and whether a partisan seat flipped, judged against whoever held it going in; null until the contest has a winner and is linked to its seat.

fetched_at.description: When we last read it from the source.

SeatChangeParty.description: One party’s seats in the selection.

slug.description: Party slug, for flipped_to= and flipped_from=.

held_going_in.description: Contests whose holders going in included this party.

won.description: Contests this party won (for vote for N, at least one seat).

gained.description: Flipped contests this party won without holding a seat up going in.

lost.description: Flipped contests this party held going in and won no seat in.

contests.description: Decided contests linked to a seat.

partisan.description: Of those, contests for partisan seats.

flip_unknown.description: Partisan seats where the holder’s or the winner’s party isn’t known, so flipped is null.

outcomes.description: Contests by seat outcome (incumbent_reelected, incumbent_defeated, open_seat, new_seat, unknown, incumbents_reelected, mixed); outcomes with none are left out.

post.summary: Look up the ballot at an address
post.description:
The ballot at a street address (or a point): the districts it is in on today’s lines, and every contest on its ballot, grouped by election, in ballot order, with each choice and how many endorsers back it. By default every election from 60 days ago on, so the latest election’s results are included; ask for others with elections. Use GET /v1/contests/{id} for each endorser’s position in a contest.

The address is found with the U.S. Census Bureau’s geocoder and matched to our districts the same way endorsedby.org does. It is sent in the body so it stays out of URLs and logs, and it is used for this request only: we never store it. Each lookup counts as one request, and an account may make up to 60 lookups a minute. Districts are matched on today’s maps, so a past election in a redistricted area can show the wrong district’s contests.

get.description:
Every endorsement change matching a subscription or inline filter, as Server-Sent Events, within seconds of it happening. Events: ready (first, with the subscription name), endorsement (an Event), checkpoint (moves your position past changes your filter skipped), reconnect (we end connections after an hour), and error (cursor_expired). A comment line arrives every 20 seconds.

Each event id is a cursor: reconnect with Last-Event-ID (EventSource does this itself) or ?cursor= to continue. Cursors work on /v1/events too. Without one you start at the newest change (from=latest); from=earliest or since= start further back. A cursor older than the stream keeps (7 days, at most 50,000 changes) ends the stream with an error event, cursor_expired, or gets 410 before it opens. There is no limit on how many streams you hold open.

The Endorsement Stream ends at the close of December 31, 2027 (Pacific).

get.description:
The same changes as GET /v1/stream, a page at a time, for servers that can’t hold a connection open (cron jobs, serverless functions, strict firewalls). Each response has the changes after your cursor that match your filter, oldest first, and a next_cursor (even when there are none): store it and send it as cursor next time. has_more means more are waiting, so call again right away. wait (up to 25 seconds) holds a request with nothing new open until a matching change arrives (long polling).

Without a cursor you start at the newest change (from=latest); from=earliest or since= start further back. Cursors work on /v1/stream too. A cursor older than the stream keeps (7 days, at most 50,000 changes) gets 410 cursor_expired: catch up with GET /v1/endorsements, then start again with from=latest.

The Endorsement Stream ends at the close of December 31, 2027 (Pacific).
